entries.name: Reviewing at growing intervals
entries.summary: The cards the schedule says are due today
entries.doesNotDo: It builds nothing you can use in a sentence. Cards make words come back on their own, and the rest of the app exists because that is not the same as knowing them.

entries.name: Audio cards you can use without looking
entries.summary: The same cards, spoken, with your eyes free
entries.trains: holding on to words while your eyes are elsewhere
entries.doesNotDo: It cannot grade itself honestly. Marking your own spoken answer while walking is the loosest grading in the app, and the schedule inherits that guesswork.

entries.name: Collecting sentences from your own reading
entries.summary: Turn sentences from what you read into cards
entries.doesNotDo: It ignores how common a word is. Words you happen to meet are not the words that unlock the most text, and collecting alone leaves common ones unlearned for years.

entries.name: Word pairs rather than single words (collocations)
entries.summary: Learn a word together with the words it usually travels with
entries.trains: fluency — the word together with what belongs to it
entries.doesNotDo: It counts as one item what is really several. A word-pair card grows your vocabulary more slowly than the same minutes on single words.

entries.name: Finishing off a group of common words
entries.summary: Work all the way through one group of the frequency list
entries.trains: how much of a text you understand
entries.doesNotDo: It chases the number rather than the need. Finishing a group is satisfying, and it can spend a week on words you would never have missed.

entries.name: Handwriting sheet of the twenty shakiest cards
entries.summary: Write out the twenty cards you keep failing
entries.doesNotDo: It is slow and it is off-app, so its result has to be typed back in or it produces no signal at all.
